speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a dermatological condition with potential oncologic implications; please describe the appearance, size, and any changes you have noticed in the affected lesion. To begin our assessment, have you experienced any itching, bleeding, or pain in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (likely multifocal, including penile and digital varieties). The patient's history of heavy smoking, non-healing lesions in unusual locations (finger shaft, penile shaft), and failed treatment for syphilis/eczema strongly suggest a malignancy rather than an infectious or inflammatory etiology. Immediate biopsy is required for confirmation.
